title: The all-witness ownership floor IS a direct combinatorial upper bound on F3 incidence I(delta)
wall: W-BGK (welds back to the analytic sub-sqrt(q) character-sum / Paley wall; the combinatorial Fisher cap is 2^Theta(n)-vacuous at the prize budget)
evidence: The brick allWitness_badScalars_card_mul_le (AllWitnessOwnershipFloor.lean, axiom-clean propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound) genuinely proves #bad*C(w0,d+1) <= C(n,d+2), i.e. I(delta) <= C(n,k+1)/C(w0,k) (d+2=k+1, d+1=k), a real character-sum-free upper bound on exactly the F3 far-line incidence. The connection's factual claim (it bounds the SAME object as F1's delta*) is CORRECT. But the attack_plan's quantitative test fails: probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/probe_C002_fast.py (log-gamma, exact, dyadic n up to 2^30, rho in {1/2,1/4,1/8,1/16}, delta at the EASIEST = smallest-cap interior of the prize window (1-sqrt rho, 1-rho-1/log n)) shows the cap is 2^Theta(n), astronomically above the prize budget q*eps* = poly(n). Concretely at n=2^30, rho=1/2, k=2^29, smallest-cap delta=0.296, w0=755835262: log2(cap)=4.17e8, while log2(budget) for q~n^beta*eps*, beta in 1..5, is only ~30-150 => the cap exceeds budget by ~4.17e8 BITS. Same conclusion at every rho and every n>=1024 (the lone negative entry n=256/rho=1/16/budget=n^5 is the #400 small-prime trap: n^5=2^40 vs cap=2^38.5, an artifact that vanishes as n grows). Sanity: the probe reproduces the in-tree concrete payoff C(16,4)/C(6,3)=91 exactly (matching level1_engine_goodSide_F12289_sharp), confirming it computes the brick's exact object; that file's own honest-scope note already states the level-1 rung needs <=31<52<=91, so the rung stays open. Structural reason the cap cannot reach budget: the Fisher/ownership argument uses ONLY pairwise-disjoint owned (d+2)-subsets (one-sided packing); reaching budget ~n would need C(w0,d+1) >= C(n,d+2)/n, false by 2^Theta(n) because the witness size w0~(1-delta)n is bounded away from n throughout the window. Distinguishing the ~O(n)/q bad scalars from the ~q good ones is precisely the analytic sqrt-cancellation among the q/n Gauss phases (BGK). This matches the DISPROOF_LOG prior art (ListIncidencePolyMethod's |L|*C(a,k)<=C(n,k) k-uniform Fisher cap, ListInteriorPinGeneral, FisherJohnsonCrossover 'neither dominates', SubgroupCharacterSumNoGo): the field-blind incidence cap is the convergent wall, the open core is the sub-sqrt(q) character sum.
honest_note: The brick is a CORRECT, axiom-clean, non-analytic upper bound on the right object (I(delta) = F3 incidence = F1 delta* object), and the connection's qualitative claim that it is a character-sum-free reverse bound on I(delta) is true. What is REFUTED is only the IMPLICIT hope (and the attack_plan's reach test) that this combinatorial bound is TIGHT enough to reach the prize budget and thereby close the prize without analytic input: it overshoots by 2^Theta(n) in the whole prize window. It is not a new wall and not a closure; it is the already-known Fisher/polynomial-method face of the existing W-Johnson/W-BGK wall, re-derived via the divided-difference ownership floor (which DOES sharpen the small-instance unconditional good side, e.g. 208/p -> 91/p at the level-1 rung, but stays vacuous at production dimension exactly as the file's own honest-scope note states). No DISPROOF_LOG entry is needed beyond noting the cap's 2^Theta(n) gap, which the existing FisherJohnsonCrossover/no-go bricks already encode. Scope: I tested the canonical prize tunings (q*eps* = poly(n), beta 1..5); I did not chase exotic eps* tunings where poly(n) could rival 2^Theta(n), since that would violate eps*=2^-128 with q a genuine prime ~n^beta.
